reviews.title: Please help!
reviews.text:
Humidifier Support Needs Significant Improvement

The ecobee app and thermostat offer very limited support for humidifier control, which defeats the purpose of having a smart thermostat.

1. No humidifier status indicator: The app and thermostat clearly show when heating or cooling is running, but there is no equivalent indicator for the humidifier. Why can’t we see when the humidifier is actually operating?

2. No humidifier scheduling: Humidity settings should be adjustable through Comfort Settings and schedules, just like temperature. For example, I don’t need the humidifier running all day when nobody is home, especially when windows are open to cool the house. However, I want it operating at night while sleeping.

Instead, I’m forced to manually turn the humidifier on and off every single day. This is exactly the kind of repetitive task a smart thermostat should eliminate.

3. Confusing humidity range: The recent change to display a humidity range instead of a specific setpoint makes things unnecessarily confusing. When exactly does the humidifier turn off—at the lower or upper end of the range? A clear target humidity setting with understandable operating thresholds would be far more useful.

These aren’t advanced features. They’re basic functionality that should already exist in a smart thermostat capable of controlling a whole-home humidifier.

When will ecobee address these limitations and provide proper humidifier status, scheduling, and control?

reviews.title: Love it…HATE that it breaks HomeKit compatibility with every update.
reviews.text:
It’s a great thermostat. When it’s working properly, that is. I don’t know when it started exactly, but every single time there’s a new update released, it completely breaks compatibility with my Apple HomeKit. What ends up happening is Siri will basically half respond and say that the thermostat is not responding when clearly it is functioning just fine, or it’ll basically half function, meaning that it’ll work, turn it on and off, but won’t work for anything else like setting the temperature. And I’m getting really sick of having to delete the thermostat from my home and delete it from the thermostat itself, pulling it out of the wall to have it do a hard reboot, as that seems to be the only way, and then repairing it. After you do so, everything works as expected until the next update. I’ve gone to the point now where I just expect every time I see an update for my thermostat that I’m going to have to re-sync all of my home kit data.

reviews.title: Power outages result in Alerts that shouldn't be.
reviews.text: For about the past three power outages, so the last few months, every time the power goes out and comes back on, it alerts me that I need to change my furnace filter. When I click into it, it tells me that I've already addressed it, I click "got it," but the alert is still there and I have to go and change the date that I actually changed the furnace filter so that it'll go away., because though it tells me I've addressed the issue, the alert doesn't go away. This shouldn't be an issue, this should be something that is kept within the system, not where it can lose that information when the power goes out. I'm the one who deals with that stuff, and my family members drive me crazy until I fix it, because it really should not even be an issue. It drives me crazy because I shouldn't have to go in and change the date back to the date that I changed it. It should already know that. Like I said, this has been just over the last few months, this wasn't something that always happened before. We've been Ecobee users for about four or five years now. This is something that could cost people money that they don't have, or shouldn't have to spend, if they can't remember what day they changed their filter, so feel the need to do it again, just because they can't remember. Think about the elderly, who may not have the memory they used to, but are still capable of doing things for themselves.
